meta.question: How do I file a response?

question: How do I file a response?

answers:
If you have received a Summons and Petition and wish to respond, you can find the necessary forms at https://www.courts.ca.gov/forms.htm. It is important to file a response, as failing to do so may result in a judgment being entered against you. 
If you agree with all or part of the requests, you can express this to the judge by completing, filing, and serving a court form that indicates your agreement or disagreement, along with your reasons. You will need to attend the hearing to present your side of the story.
Generally, there is no cost to respond; however, if this is your first time filing papers in this case, there may be a fee. If you cannot afford the fee, you can request a fee waiver.
If you decide to respond, you must complete and serve your response to the other party at least 9 court days before the hearing. For step-by-step instructions on how to file a response and prepare for the hearing, please refer to the available resources.

history.content: What is the procedure to schedule an ex-parte hearing?

Here are the steps to follow:
1. Reserve a hearing date with the applicable department. Ex parte reservations cannot be obtained via the portal and must be obtained from the courtroom.
2. File the motion with the court.
3. Give notice of the hearing date as required by law.
1. Submit the ex parte application via drop box at least 24 hours in advance of the desired ex parte hearing date and time.
2. Provide the noticed party(ies) with the noticed date and time, a copy of the ex parte application, and a written advisement to submit any written response or objections by using the drop box by 8:30 am on the day of the ex parte hearing.
3. File with the court via drop box a completed declaration showing that the noticed party(ies) was served with the notice of the date and time of ex parte hearing, a copy of the ex parte application, and a copy of the written advisement to the noticed party(ies) re the submission of written response or objections, at least 24 hours in advance of the ex parte hearing date.
4. Provide current telephone numbers for all parties for potential Zoom telepresence appearance and/or hearing.
Please note that ex parte relief may only be granted upon a showing of irreparable harm or immediate danger.
What happens when the Judicial Officer makes a ruling?

A court representative will prepare the orders and documents after the Judicial Officer makes a ruling in an ex parte hearing. These will be made available by pick-up from the drop box or attorney box. Parties are required to comply with any service requirements post the ex parte hearing and to submit proof of service to the court before the return hearing.
I do not have information on what tentative rulings are.
How Do I Find a Tentative Ruling?

To find a tentative ruling, you can search by department number or by case number through the eCourt Public Portal. Here are the steps:
1. Log into eCourt Public Portal
2. Case Search
3. Enter the Case Number and select "Search"
4. Select the Case Name
5. Select the Tentative Rulings Tab
6. Select "View"
In some cases, such as recently filed unlawful detainer (eviction) cases, tentative rulings may only be available by telephone.
What does it mean to receive a Request for Order?

If you received a Request for Order (form FL-300), it means that the other party in your family law case is asking the judge to make a decision. The court will schedule a hearing date to allow both sides to present their arguments before the judge makes a decision.
If you are served personally, you must be served with the documents at least 16 court days before the hearing. If you are served by mail, you must be served at least 16 court days plus an additional 5 calendar days before the hearing.
Thank you for informing me; I was not aware of that.
You're welcome! I'm glad I could help. If you have any more questions, feel free to ask.
